PREMIUM UI & FRONTEND DESIGN SYSTEM

GENERAL PRINCIPLE

Build production-quality interfaces that feel intentionally designed by an
experienced product designer and frontend engineer.

Do not produce generic AI-generated SaaS interfaces.

Prioritize:

- strong visual hierarchy
- excellent typography
- intentional spacing
- distinctive composition
- clear information architecture
- coherent design tokens
- responsive behavior
- accessibility
- meaningful interaction design
- purposeful micro-interactions
- polished loading, empty, success, and error states

The interface should feel designed, not decorated.

DESIGN PROCESS

Before making substantial UI changes:

1. Inspect the existing interface.
2. Identify existing design tokens.
3. Identify existing typography.
4. Identify existing colors.
5. Identify spacing and layout patterns.
6. Identify reusable components.
7. Determine whether the request requires refinement or redesign.
8. Preserve existing functionality unless explicitly asked to change it.

Do not blindly redesign existing interfaces.

VISUAL QUALITY

Avoid generic AI/SaaS patterns unless they are genuinely appropriate for the
product.

Avoid:

- purple-to-blue gradients
- unnecessary gradients
- gradient text
- excessive glassmorphism
- glowing UI
- excessive rounded cards
- nested cards
- card grids everywhere
- excessive shadows
- excessive pills
- excessive badges
- decorative icons without purpose
- random blobs
- neon effects
- everything-centered layouts
- repetitive sections
- oversized headings without purpose
- huge empty areas
- tiny low-contrast text
- generic dashboard templates
- arbitrary animations
- decorative charts with no product purpose

Do not add decoration merely to make the interface look "premium."

PREMIUM DESIGN

Premium quality comes from:

- typography
- spacing
- hierarchy
- composition
- consistency
- restraint
- interaction quality
- meaningful visual details

Prefer distinctive design decisions over safe template-like layouts.

TYPOGRAPHY

Treat typography as a primary design element.

Create a deliberate type hierarchy:

- display
- heading
- subheading
- body
- supporting text
- labels
- metadata
- buttons

Do not use one font size everywhere.

Do not make body text unnecessarily small.

Do not automatically default to Inter or Roboto.

Choose typography based on the product's personality and audience.

COLOR

Use semantic color tokens.

Prefer:

- background
- surface
- surface-elevated
- foreground
- foreground-muted
- border
- primary
- primary-hover
- secondary
- success
- warning
- danger

Do not introduce colors randomly.

Maintain accessible contrast.

LAYOUT

Use a deliberate spacing system.

Maintain:

- alignment
- rhythm
- hierarchy
- appropriate content width
- responsive behavior
- comfortable touch targets

Do not give every element identical spacing.

RESPONSIVE DESIGN

Design mobile intentionally.

Do not simply shrink the desktop layout.

Check:

- navigation
- typography
- spacing
- forms
- tables
- cards
- dialogs
- touch targets
- overflow
- images
- content hierarchy

ACCESSIBILITY

Accessibility is part of design quality.

Check:

- semantic HTML
- keyboard navigation
- focus states
- contrast
- labels
- form errors
- touch targets
- reduced motion
- screen-reader meaning

MOTION

Use animation only when it improves:

- comprehension
- feedback
- hierarchy
- perceived quality

Prefer subtle, intentional motion.

Do not animate everything.

COMPONENTS

Prefer reusable components and design tokens.

Before creating a new component:

1. Check whether an existing component can be reused.
2. Extend an existing component when appropriate.
3. Avoid duplicate components with slightly different styling.

CONTENT

Never use Lorem ipsum.

Use realistic product copy.

Avoid vague placeholder text when meaningful copy can be written.

FINAL UI QUALITY CHECK

Before considering substantial UI work complete:

1. Check visual hierarchy.
2. Check typography.
3. Check spacing.
4. Check colors and contrast.
5. Check responsive behavior.
6. Check hover/focus/active/disabled states.
7. Check loading/empty/error states.
8. Check accessibility.
9. Remove unnecessary decoration.
10. Check for generic AI UI patterns.
11. Polish the final result.

When the task involves UI design, redesign, critique, auditing, typography,
layout, color, motion, accessibility, or visual polish, use the Impeccable
design workflow when available.

QUALITY BAR

Do not stop at "functional."

The result should be:

- production-ready
- coherent
- distinctive
- responsive
- accessible
- visually refined
- consistent with the product's design language
